result.markdown:
For a small company, my top recommendation would be **BambooHR for managing employees and HR**, or **Rippling if you want to automate more of your business operations**\.

However, the best choice depends on whether you need payroll, hiring, employee records, performance reviews, time-off tracking, or all of these.

Here are the platforms I'd shortlist for 2026.

Best for companies wanting a proper HR department in one platform.

Pricing: Quote-based; reported starting rates around \$10/employee/month, with minimums.

## My recommendation if your company is in Canada

I'd narrow the list to these three\:

| Software | Best use |
|--------|--------|
| **Employment Hero (formerly Humi)** | All-in-one Canadian HR and payroll |
| **Rise People** | Affordable HR, payroll and benefits |
| **Collage HR** | Employee management, onboarding and HR processes |


These are particularly worth considering because Canadian payroll involves CRA remittances, CPP, EI, T4s and Records of Employment. US-focused products like Gusto aren't a suitable standalone Canadian payroll solution. search_results.description: TechRadar’s 2026 guide evaluates leading HR software for payroll, compliance, recruitment, onboarding, benefits, performance management, and employee administration. Gusto is named best overall for its full-service payroll, time tracking, benefits administration, compliance support, and HR guidance. Employment Hero is recommended for small and medium-sized businesses because of its customizable workflows, automation, AI assistant, and broad feature set, though advanced functions and add-ons can increase costs. Rippling is best for versatility, particularly for distributed teams, offering remote device management, tax registration, scalable services, and per-employee billing. Other recommendations include Remote Payroll for international enterprises, BambooHR as an all-in-one system, Zoho People for integrations, Breathe HR for simple employee management, Deel for powerful global HR capabilities, PeopleHR for mobile access, Paylocity for mid-sized businesses, Staffology Payroll for complex enterprise payroll, Workable for recruitment, and BrightHR for extensive workforce-management features. The guide advises selecting software according to company size and specific workflow needs, and explains that testing considered usability, features, security, support, pricing, and user feedback.
